enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
528 AM MST Sun Nov 22 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 454 AM MST Sun Nov 22 2026

 - Freezing temperatures will work their way into parts of the
   desert lowlands tonight into Sunday morning.

 - A weak upper level disturbance arriving Monday night is
   trending a little stronger, and could produce some light snow
   in the Sacramento Mountains, ending Tuesday morning.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 941 PM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

The upper trough is exiting the area, with the Pacific cold front
also well to our east. Winds have diminished and shifted to the
NNW as expected, with cooler, drier air filtering in. Some high
clouds over southern Arizona will drift across northern sections
of the CWA overnight, but will do little to affect temperatures. 
The usual cold spots in the Gila have already dropped into the
20s. In the lowlands, it's already 34 near Hachita, and 32 along
US-180 in NW Luna County. Some upper-30s are starting to pop up in
Sierra and Dona Ana County as well.

The Freeze Warning was expanded into southern Dona Ana County
earlier this shift, after noting locally-generated bias-corrected
NBM grids continued to show lows below freezing between Mesilla
and La Union. Many of these areas managed to drop to the 33 to 35
range last night and this morning. Winds will be a little more 
active tonight versus last night, but dewpoints will drop into the
20s, with weak cold advection. This all favors a light freeze in
the lower elevations of the Mesilla Valley, but expect a quick
jump into the upper-30s with a little elevation rise.

A slight wrinkle in the mid-term forecast, as some models and
ensemble members have trended deeper with the fast-moving upper
trough expected to pass through the area Monday night. The GFS
grazes northern Otero County with some light precipitation, while
the RRFS is much deeper and stronger, with precip (rain) as far
south as El Paso late Monday night into Tuesday morning, and QPF
supportive of a 2-3 inches of snow in the Sacramento Mountains.
That seems a little extreme, and with the RRFS's short track 
record, a more measured approach is best. For now, 30 to 50 PoPs
mainly for the Sacramento Mountains, and up to an inch of snow in
the grids, with snow levels down to about 7500 feet on the west
slopes, and 5500 feet on the east slopes.  

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 525 AM MST Sun Nov 22 2026

VFR conditions for the next 24 hours. We had breezy winds
yesterday, but today will see less winds. Our winds today will
come around to the east by noon and then become light and variable
tonight. Our ceilings will be unlimited today and tonight. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 525 AM MST Sun Nov 22 2026

The upper level storm system that gave us breezy conditions on
Saturday was moving away from the region and a little cooler and
less windy weather pattern has settled over the region. Our min
RH's will stay at or above 20% today through Friday, but we will
see a chance for light snow showers in the Sacramento Mountains
late Monday night. The rest of the week looks dry with high
temperatures running a few degrees below average.

&&
